1. **"Getting Away with Murder"** refers to the 2004 album by rock band **Papa Roach** (which performed that song and released it as a single).

2. **Papa Roach was formed in Vacaville, California** (a small Northern California town near Sacramento).

3. **Veoh's headquarters** was in **San Diego**, California (confirmed by multiple sources including NBC News which stated "The San Diego-based company has raised $12.5 million").

4. Among California's **top five largest cities by population**:
   - 1. Los Angeles (~3.87 million)
   - 2. **San Diego** (~1.41 million)
   - 3. San Jose (~990,000)
   - 4. San Francisco (~826,000)
   - 5. Fresno (~555,000)

**Answer: Veoh's headquarters city (San Diego) ranks #2 among the top five largest cities in California.**

_**Getting Away with Murder**_ is the fourth studio album by American rock band Papa Roach. The album was a departure from the band's previous works, showcasing an alternative rock and hard rock sound instead of a nu metal and rap metal sound. Unlike their previous albums, the album features no rapping and instead only features Jacoby Shaddix singing. It was released on August 31, 2004, via Geffen Records and has been certified Gold in Canada, Silver in the United Kingdom and Platinum in the United States. _Getting Away with Murder_ peaked at number 17 on the _Billboard_ 200.
Production lasted from October to December 2003. During the recording of _Getting Away with Murder_, the band was not signed to a label as their previous label DreamWorks Records had recently been bought out. The band would later sign to Geffen Records. The album features a departure from the band's rap metal sound, as the band's vocalist Jacoby Shaddix stated that he was tired of rapping.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Getting_Away_with_Murder_(album)#cite_note-6)
The track "Just Go (Never Look Back)" was recorded in the album's sessions, but was ultimately left off the album.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Getting_Away_with_Murder_(album)#cite_note-7) The track would later be released on the band's future greatest hits album, _...To Be Loved: The Best of Papa Roach_.

Papa Roach released _Getting Away with Murder_ on August 31, 2004. The album's first single was the title track. The album debuted at number 17 on the _Billboard_ 200, with 52,000 copies sold, less than a half of _Lovehatetragedy_. However, the title track saw success through radio and peaked at number two in the Mainstream Rock Tracks chart, number four on the Modern Rock Tracks and number 69 on the _Billboard_ Hot 100. The second single, "Scars", peaked at number four on the Mainstream Rock Tracks chart, number two on the Modern Rock Tracks chart, number 15 on the _Billboard_ Hot 100, and number seven on the Pop Songs chart, becoming the band's biggest hit in the United States. "Scars" was ranked at number 36 as the greatest song of 2005 and as the most successful song of the year by _Billboard_, becoming the band's first and only song to be included on _Billboard_'s year-end charts, in addition, "Scars" was the band's first song to crossover to top 40 radio since their breakthrough hit, "Last Resort". The song "Take Me" also charted on the Modern Rock Tracks chart (at number 23), and on the Mainstream Rock Tracks chart (at number 11) despite not being released as a single. To support the album, the band toured throughout 2004 and 2005. _Getting Away with Murder_ eventually achieved a Platinum certification in the United States, after spending 61 weeks on the _Billboard_ 200 thanks to the hit of "Scars", outselling _Lovehatetragedy_. It is their second best-selling album after their debut _Infest_, also their first and only album to have at least two Hot 100 hits.

Several other tracks were used to promote the album across various mediums. The track "Blood (Empty Promises)" was featured on the _Saw II_soundtrack and the track "Getting Away with Murder" was featured in the end credits of _The Chronicles of Riddick_, as well as the video games _MechAssault 2: Lone Wolf_ and _MX vs. ATV Unleashed_. "Not Listening" was used in the trailer for _Resident Evil: Apocalypse_ and is also featured in the video games _NASCAR 2005: Chase for the Cup_, _Gran Turismo 4_, and _FlatOut 2_.

The band would later sign to Geffen Records. The album features a departure from the band's rap metal sound, as the band's vocalist Jacoby Shaddix stated that he was tired of rapping.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Getting_Away_with_Murder_(album)#cite_note-6)

texts.2: Papa Roach released _Getting Away with Murder_ on August 31, 2004. The album's first single was the title track. Papa Roach -- a world-touring, Grammy-nominated, triple-platinum rock band with members who originally hail from Vacaville – will break away from their album promotion schedule on May 3 to come home to deliver a message to Solano County children: Be fearless, dream big, aim high to develop your full creative potential.
Papa Roach formed in 1993, with Jacoby Shaddix, a student at Vacaville High, and Jerry Horton of Vanden High, since that time and with Members Tobin Esperance and Tony Palermo, Papa Roach have achieved critical and commercial acclaim selling over 25 million albums worldwide. The band is currently set to release their ninth studio album, “Crooked Teeth,” on May 19, and their current single, “Help,” is No. 1 on rock radio.
Members of the band will return to their hometown for a special dedication ceremony at Imagine That! – Vacaville’s newly opened hands-on learning Exploratorium for children of all ages and abilities. Exhibits at the center encourage children to be free to imagine, create, and welcome sciences and art into their lives. Portions of this exhibit have been generously supported by The Shaddix Family Charitable Fund through NorthBay Healthcare Foundation. Established in 2014 by Jacoby and wife Kelly Shaddix, the fund has also been used to support NorthBay Hospice and Bereavement, the new NorthBay Cancer Center in Vacaville and numerous children’s educational endeavors and scholarship funds.
The highlight of this special ceremony will be Vacaville Mayor Len Augustine proclaiming May 3 as Papa Roach Day in Vacaville. In honor of Papa Roach’s generous support of our community, organizers have created a special exhibit at the center that celebrates their musical success. One portion of the exhibit invites youngsters to play out their rock dreams and musical talents. The dedication will take place from 4 p.m. to 5:30 p.m. on Wednesday, May 3 at Vacaville’s Imagine That!, 848-B Alamo Drive.

The Papa Roach dedication falls just days before the band releases their latest album, “Crooked Teeth,” which is also available for pre-order at paparoach.com. Priceless autographed memorabilia, a raffle and door prizes will be available at the dedication. With very special thanks to Lauren Runow, Imagine That! Founder, the event is open to everyone and all regular admission fees will be waived.
Please join us to celebrate and honor the inspiring beginnings of Papa Roach, whose selflessness through music have enriched the lives of others and highlighted the importance of community.

## With very special guests Sixx:A.M. and support from From Ashes To New
Los Angeles, CA, June 13, 2016 - With 10 #1 singles and over 25 Top 10 singles between them, millions of video streams and fans all over the globe, FIVE FINGER DEATH PUNCH and PAPA ROACH have been dominating the airwaves throughout their careers. Both bands—who have been heralded, by fans and press alike, as having killer live shows—have come together to co-headline Canadian arenas from coast to coast for the first time this fall, presented by Mascioli Entertainment and Evenko with $1 of each ticket sold being donated to a wildfire relief charity organization soon to be announced. See the tour dates further below and watch a special teaser previewing the Canadian Tour below!
Video 3
Exclusive 5FDP/PR demand ticket & VIP pre-sale start -Tuesday 6/14, 10:00am EST
HMV Exclusive Pre-sale - Wednesday 6/15, 10:00am EST
Local venue & radio pre-sale kick off -Thursday, 6/16, 10am local time
General Public Onsale - Friday, 6/17, 10am local time
For tickets, more info and details on FIVE FINGER DEATH PUNCH, PAPA ROACH and SIXX:A.M. VIP package offerings, go to http://www.fivefingerdeathpunch.com/tour and http://paparoach.com/events and http://sixxammusic.com
Says Mike Mascioli, CEO of Mascioli Entertainment: “I will never lose my passion for buying and promoting national tours, especially when bands like Five Finger Death Punch and Papa Roach stay loyal by sticking with independents like myself. And with the massive success of this same tour in the States and Europe, I'm thrilled to be able to bring them to Canada!" Daniel Glick, Director of Concerts & Events for Evenko adds: “Fans spoke and we listened. We worked really hard with both bands to make this happen. They’ve been on our must-have list for a while now and announcing this tour is very exciting. We look forward to seeing Five Finger Death Punch and Papa Roach this fall in Canada”.

## With very special guests Sixx:A.M. and support from From Ashes To New
FIVE FINGER DEATH PUNCH and PAPA ROACH actively involved the fans by giving them the opportunity to request the tour come to their city via a “demand campaign” housed at http://demand.fivefingerdeathpunch.com/ and http://demand.paparoach.com/
An overwhelming 60,000 Canadian fans responded to the call to action and made their voices heard.
Zoltan Bathory (guitar) of FIVE FINGER DEATH PUNCH states: “We took this Demand Campaign everywhere. We had huge success with it in the USA, and in Europe it even won the “Arena Tour Of The Year” award… It’s not surprising in a way as it is inclusive of the fans - they vote and we are listening. What a concept, right? Nobody learns from talking, you learn from listening.”
“When we did this tour last year in the USA, it was truly the Best Tour Ever. We heard from so many of our Canadian fans that really wanted to see this show – so we’re bringing it to them. Really cannot be more excited to go back – even heading east of Quebec. This is one show you won’t wanna miss.” says PAPA ROACH vocalist, Jacoby Shaddix.
FIVE FINGER DEATH PUNCH AND PAPA ROACH previously co-headlined American and European arenas to great success last Fall and won the prestigious “Arena Tour Of The Year” award from the German Promoters Association.
Special guests on the tour will be SIXX:A.M., whose single, “Rise” is currently #3 on the Canadian Rock Chart. Their recent April 29 global release of Prayers For The Damned, Vol. 1, debuted at #1 on the US Independent Album Chart, #2 on the US Rock Albums Chart, #7 on Canada’s Billboard Top 200 Chart, and in the Top 5 Album Chart around the globe. Vocalist James Michael says: "We've been getting tremendous support for our new single “Rise” from the fans and from Canadian radio. We are thrilled to be touring Canada this fall with FFDP and Papa Roach!"

Papa Roach -- a world-touring, Grammy-nominated, triple-platinum rock band with members who originally hail from Vacaville – will break away from their album promotion schedule on May 3 to come home to deliver a message to Solano County children: Be fearless, dream big, aim high to develop your full creative potential.
Papa Roach formed in 1993, with Jacoby Shaddix, a student at Vacaville High, and Jerry Horton of Vanden High, since that time and with Members Tobin Esperance and Tony Palermo, Papa Roach have achieved critical and commercial acclaim selling over 25 million albums worldwide. The band is currently set to release their ninth studio album, “Crooked Teeth,” on May 19, and their current single, “Help,” is No. 1 on rock radio.
Members of the band will return to their hometown for a special dedication ceremony at Imagine That! – Vacaville’s newly opened hands-on learning Exploratorium for children of all ages and abilities. Exhibits at the center encourage children to be free to imagine, create, and welcome sciences and art into their lives. Portions of this exhibit have been generously supported by The Shaddix Family Charitable Fund through NorthBay Healthcare Foundation. Established in 2014 by Jacoby and wife Kelly Shaddix, the fund has also been used to support NorthBay Hospice and Bereavement, the new NorthBay Cancer Center in Vacaville and numerous children’s educational endeavors and scholarship funds.
The highlight of this special ceremony will be Vacaville Mayor Len Augustine proclaiming May 3 as Papa Roach Day in Vacaville. In honor of Papa Roach’s generous support of our community, organizers have created a special exhibit at the center that celebrates their musical success. One portion of the exhibit invites youngsters to play out their rock dreams and musical talents. The dedication will take place from 4 p.m. to 5:30 p.m. on Wednesday, May 3 at Vacaville’s Imagine That!, 848-B Alamo Drive.

Please join us to celebrate and honor the inspiring beginnings of Papa Roach, whose selflessness through music have enriched the lives of others and highlighted the importance of community.

## With very special guests Sixx:A.M. and support from From Ashes To New
Los Angeles, CA, June 13, 2016 - With 10 #1 singles and over 25 Top 10 singles between them, millions of video streams and fans all over the globe, FIVE FINGER DEATH PUNCH and PAPA ROACH have been dominating the airwaves throughout their careers. Both bands—who have been heralded, by fans and press alike, as having killer live shows—have come together to co-headline Canadian arenas from coast to coast for the first time this fall, presented by Mascioli Entertainment and Evenko with $1 of each ticket sold being donated to a wildfire relief charity organization soon to be announced. See the tour dates further below and watch a special teaser previewing the Canadian Tour below!

HMV Exclusive Pre-sale - Wednesday 6/15, 10:00am EST
Local venue & radio pre-sale kick off -Thursday, 6/16, 10am local time
General Public Onsale - Friday, 6/17, 10am local time
For tickets, more info and details on FIVE FINGER DEATH PUNCH, PAPA ROACH and SIXX:A.M. VIP package offerings, go to http://www.fivefingerdeathpunch.com/tour and http://paparoach.com/events and http://sixxammusic.com
Says Mike Mascioli, CEO of Mascioli Entertainment: “I will never lose my passion for buying and promoting national tours, especially when bands like Five Finger Death Punch and Papa Roach stay loyal by sticking with independents like myself. And with the massive success of this same tour in the States and Europe, I'm thrilled to be able to bring them to Canada!" Daniel Glick, Director of Concerts & Events for Evenko adds: “Fans spoke and we listened. We worked really hard with both bands to make this happen. They’ve been on our must-have list for a while now and announcing this tour is very exciting. We look forward to seeing Five Finger Death Punch and Papa Roach this fall in Canada”.

## With very special guests Sixx:A.M. and support from From Ashes To New
FIVE FINGER DEATH PUNCH and PAPA ROACH actively involved the fans by giving them the opportunity to request the tour come to their city via a “demand campaign” housed at http://demand.fivefingerdeathpunch.com/ and http://demand.paparoach.com/
An overwhelming 60,000 Canadian fans responded to the call to action and made their voices heard.
Zoltan Bathory (guitar) of FIVE FINGER DEATH PUNCH states: “We took this Demand Campaign everywhere. We had huge success with it in the USA, and in Europe it even won the “Arena Tour Of The Year” award… It’s not surprising in a way as it is inclusive of the fans - they vote and we are listening. What a concept, right? Nobody learns from talking, you learn from listening.”
“When we did this tour last year in the USA, it was truly the Best Tour Ever. We heard from so many of our Canadian fans that really wanted to see this show – so we’re bringing it to them. Really cannot be more excited to go back – even heading east of Quebec. This is one show you won’t wanna miss.” says PAPA ROACH vocalist, Jacoby Shaddix.
FIVE FINGER DEATH PUNCH AND PAPA ROACH previously co-headlined American and European arenas to great success last Fall and won the prestigious “Arena Tour Of The Year” award from the German Promoters Association.
Special guests on the tour will be SIXX:A.M., whose single, “Rise” is currently #3 on the Canadian Rock Chart. Their recent April 29 global release of Prayers For The Damned, Vol. 1, debuted at #1 on the US Independent Album Chart, #2 on the US Rock Albums Chart, #7 on Canada’s Billboard Top 200 Chart, and in the Top 5 Album Chart around the globe. Vocalist James Michael says: "We've been getting tremendous support for our new single “Rise” from the fans and from Canadian radio. We are thrilled to be touring Canada this fall with FFDP and Papa Roach!"

Papa Roach -- a world-touring, Grammy-nominated, triple-platinum rock band with members who originally hail from Vacaville – will break away from their album promotion schedule on May 3 to come home to deliver a message to Solano County children: Be fearless, dream big, aim high to develop your full creative potential.
Papa Roach formed in 1993, with Jacoby Shaddix, a student at Vacaville High, and Jerry Horton of Vanden High, since that time and with Members Tobin Esperance and Tony Palermo, Papa Roach have achieved critical and commercial acclaim selling over 25 million albums worldwide. The band is currently set to release their ninth studio album, “Crooked Teeth,” on May 19, and their current single, “Help,” is No. 1 on rock radio.
Members of the band will return to their hometown for a special dedication ceremony at Imagine That! – Vacaville’s newly opened hands-on learning Exploratorium for children of all ages and abilities. Exhibits at the center encourage children to be free to imagine, create, and welcome sciences and art into their lives. Portions of this exhibit have been generously supported by The Shaddix Family Charitable Fund through NorthBay Healthcare Foundation. Established in 2014 by Jacoby and wife Kelly Shaddix, the fund has also been used to support NorthBay Hospice and Bereavement, the new NorthBay Cancer Center in Vacaville and numerous children’s educational endeavors and scholarship funds.
The highlight of this special ceremony will be Vacaville Mayor Len Augustine proclaiming May 3 as Papa Roach Day in Vacaville. In honor of Papa Roach’s generous support of our community, organizers have created a special exhibit at the center that celebrates their musical success. One portion of the exhibit invites youngsters to play out their rock dreams and musical talents. The dedication will take place from 4 p.m. to 5:30 p.m. on Wednesday, May 3 at Vacaville’s Imagine That!, 848-B Alamo Drive.

The Papa Roach dedication falls just days before the band releases their latest album, “Crooked Teeth,” which is also available for pre-order at paparoach.com. Priceless autographed memorabilia, a raffle and door prizes will be available at the dedication. With very special thanks to Lauren Runow, Imagine That! Founder, the event is open to everyone and all regular admission fees will be waived.

## About Veoh
Veoh Networks positioned itself as an internet television service, founded in 2004 by Dmitry Shapiro and officially launched in February 2007. Shapiro, a Russian immigrant with a background in electrical engineering and web development, previously founded the cybersecurity firm Akonix Systems. The idea for Veoh reportedly came to him during his honeymoon in November 2004, months before YouTube's launch, with the vision of enabling anyone to broadcast video online.
The company's platform was designed to distribute high-quality, long-format videos, aggregating content from major media companies like CBS and ABC alongside independent productions and user-generated material. It distinguished itself from competitors like YouTube by focusing on a downloadable application that organized videos, similar to an iTunes for video, and facilitated a lean-back, television-like viewing experience. This required users to install software, which presented a hurdle to adoption compared to browser-based streaming. Veoh's business model relied on advertising, with plans for behaviorally targeted ads based on users' viewing habits.
Veoh attracted significant attention and approximately $70 million in funding from prominent investors, including Time Warner, Intel Capital, Goldman Sachs, and former Disney CEO Michael Eisner, who also joined the board. At its peak, the service drew over 28 million unique monthly users. However, the company faced substantial challenges. A major lawsuit was filed by Universal Music Group (UMG) in 2007 over copyright infringement. Although Veoh ultimately won the case and subsequent appeals, with courts affirming its protections under the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA), the prolonged legal battle drained the company's financial resources. High operational costs, reportedly up to $4 million a month, combined with the economic downturn and the lawsuit's financial strain, proved unsustainable. In February 2010, Veoh filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy. The company was acquired by Qlipso in April 2010 and later by Japanese firm FC2 in 2013, before announcing it would shut down on November 11, 2024, with its content library being moved to FC2 Video.

# Veoh launches Web video syndication service
Veoh Networks Inc. is launching a Web video syndication service Tuesday that uses peer-to-peer technology to distribute DVD-quality video and publish it on the Web's most popular sites, including MySpace and YouTube.
Share
Add NBC News to Google
Feb. 12, 2007, 11:48 PM UTC / Source: The Associated Press
By By Gary Gentile
Veoh Networks Inc. is launching a Web video syndication service Tuesday that uses peer-to-peer technology to distribute DVD-quality video and publish it on the Web's most popular sites, including MySpace and YouTube.
The privately held company hopes to become an online television service, allowing content creators to build their own channels and viewers to easily find and download video.
Veoh hopes to distinguish itself from competitors such as Brightcove, Revver and others by the use of a peer-to-peer network that will allow the delivery of huge video files more efficiently. With Veoh, users share the load of transmitting content, which is generally sent in small chunks from PCs that have its software installed.
The company is also touting its virtual digital video recorder service, which allows users to subscribe to programs or download video from any Web site.
The San Diego-based company has raised $12.5 million from investors such as Michael Eisner, former chief executive of The Walt Disney Co., Time Warner Inc. and private venture capital firms.
Once content creators upload their videos to Veoh, the content can be instantly syndicated across the Web to popular sites such as YouTube and Facebook. The videos also can be distributed to blogs, Really Simply Syndication feeds and portable devices such as Apple Inc.'s iPods.
The site has already signed deals with US Weekly magazine to create a celebrity news channel. The Hollywood talent agency UTA also has agreed to create a channel to audition clips from aspiring filmmakers and actors.
The service allows content creators the flexibility to include advertising in their shows or sell clips on a rental or download-to-own basis. Users also could be charged a subscription for a season's worth of programs.
Veoh Chief Executive Dmitry Shapiro calls his service a "virtual cable operator," that can support an unlimited number of channels.

## About Veoh
Veoh Networks positioned itself as an internet television service, founded in 2004 by Dmitry Shapiro and officially launched in February 2007. Shapiro, a Russian immigrant with a background in electrical engineering and web development, previously founded the cybersecurity firm Akonix Systems. The idea for Veoh reportedly came to him during his honeymoon in November 2004, months before YouTube's launch, with the vision of enabling anyone to broadcast video online.
The company's platform was designed to distribute high-quality, long-format videos, aggregating content from major media companies like CBS and ABC alongside independent productions and user-generated material. It distinguished itself from competitors like YouTube by focusing on a downloadable application that organized videos, similar to an iTunes for video, and facilitated a lean-back, television-like viewing experience. This required users to install software, which presented a hurdle to adoption compared to browser-based streaming. Veoh's business model relied on advertising, with plans for behaviorally targeted ads based on users' viewing habits.
Veoh attracted significant attention and approximately $70 million in funding from prominent investors, including Time Warner, Intel Capital, Goldman Sachs, and former Disney CEO Michael Eisner, who also joined the board. At its peak, the service drew over 28 million unique monthly users. However, the company faced substantial challenges. A major lawsuit was filed by Universal Music Group (UMG) in 2007 over copyright infringement. Although Veoh ultimately won the case and subsequent appeals, with courts affirming its protections under the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA), the prolonged legal battle drained the company's financial resources. High operational costs, reportedly up to $4 million a month, combined with the economic downturn and the lawsuit's financial strain, proved unsustainable. In February 2010, Veoh filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy. The company was acquired by Qlipso in April 2010 and later by Japanese firm FC2 in 2013, before announcing it would shut down on November 11, 2024, with its content library being moved to FC2 Video.

# Veoh launches Web video syndication service
Veoh Networks Inc. is launching a Web video syndication service Tuesday that uses peer-to-peer technology to distribute DVD-quality video and publish it on the Web's most popular sites, including MySpace and YouTube.
Share

Feb. 12, 2007, 11:48 PM UTC / Source: The Associated Press
By By Gary Gentile
Veoh Networks Inc. is launching a Web video syndication service Tuesday that uses peer-to-peer technology to distribute DVD-quality video and publish it on the Web's most popular sites, including MySpace and YouTube.
The privately held company hopes to become an online television service, allowing content creators to build their own channels and viewers to easily find and download video.
Veoh hopes to distinguish itself from competitors such as Brightcove, Revver and others by the use of a peer-to-peer network that will allow the delivery of huge video files more efficiently. With Veoh, users share the load of transmitting content, which is generally sent in small chunks from PCs that have its software installed.
The company is also touting its virtual digital video recorder service, which allows users to subscribe to programs or download video from any Web site.
The San Diego-based company has raised $12.5 million from investors such as Michael Eisner, former chief executive of The Walt Disney Co., Time Warner Inc. and private venture capital firms.
Once content creators upload their videos to Veoh, the content can be instantly syndicated across the Web to popular sites such as YouTube and Facebook. The videos also can be distributed to blogs, Really Simply Syndication feeds and portable devices such as Apple Inc.'s iPods.
The site has already signed deals with US Weekly magazine to create a celebrity news channel. The Hollywood talent agency UTA also has agreed to create a channel to audition clips from aspiring filmmakers and actors.
The service allows content creators the flexibility to include advertising in their shows or sell clips on a rental or download-to-own basis. Users also could be charged a subscription for a season's worth of programs.
Veoh Chief Executive Dmitry Shapiro calls his service a "virtual cable operator," that can support an unlimited number of channels.

High operational costs, reportedly up to $4 million a month, combined with the economic downturn and the lawsuit's financial strain, proved unsustainable. In February 2010, Veoh filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy. The company was acquired by Qlipso in April 2010 and later by Japanese firm FC2 in 2013, before announcing it would shut down on November 11, 2024, with its content library being moved to FC2 Video.

About California
California is home to one of the most intricate systems of local governance in the country, reflecting its vast size and diverse population. The state boasts 58 counties and 482 incorporated municipalities, which include both cities and towns. California’s cities range from global metropolises like Los Angeles to small rural towns such as Dorris in Siskiyou County (population under 1,000). Each municipality functions according to its size, resources, and legal structure, providing services that range from police and fire protection to public transportation and infrastructure.
Charter cities have the authority to govern themselves according to their own charters, granting them more control over local matters like taxation, land use, and public works. Examples of charter cities include San Francisco and Los Angeles. Los Angeles, with a population of approximately 3.9 million, operates a vast range of services, including the Los Angeles Police Department (LAPD), LA Metro, and the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP).
General Law cities are governed by state law, general law cities have more limited legislative authority compared to charter cities. Examples of general law cities include Oxnard and Chico. While they manage local services like law enforcement and zoning, their ability to legislate independently is restricted.

In contrast, general law cities are governed by state law and must adhere to the state’s general statutes. Smaller cities like Oxnard (population around 200,000) or Chico (population around 100,000) fall under this category. While they manage local services like law enforcement and zoning, their capacity to legislate independently is more limited than charter cities.
Beyond cities, California has a large number of unincorporated areas where no municipal government exists. These regions, often found in rural and suburban areas, are governed directly by their respective counties. For example, in Los Angeles County, unincorporated areas such as East Los Angeles (population over 120,000) depend on the county for services like policing (provided by the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department) and road maintenance.
Special districts also play a critical role in California‘s local governance, providing specific services across city and county boundaries. These districts, such as the East Bay Municipal Utility District or the Orange County Fire Authority, ensure that essential services like water, sewage, and fire protection are managed across both urban and rural areas, regardless of municipal boundaries.
Additionally, California‘s unincorporated regions, particularly in the San Joaquin Valley and parts of Inyo County and Modoc County, are often agricultural lands that rely on county governance for law enforcement and infrastructure. For instance, Mono County manages roadways and emergency services in remote areas near the Eastern Sierra, where population density is too low to support formal municipalities.

In contrast, general law cities are governed by state law and must adhere to the state’s general statutes. Smaller cities like Oxnard (population around 200,000) or Chico (population around 100,000) fall under this category. While they manage local services like law enforcement and zoning, their capacity to legislate independently is more limited than charter cities.
Beyond cities, California has a large number of unincorporated areas where no municipal government exists. These regions, often found in rural and suburban areas, are governed directly by their respective counties. For example, in Los Angeles County, unincorporated areas such as East Los Angeles (population over 120,000) depend on the county for services like policing (provided by the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department) and road maintenance.
Special districts also play a critical role in California‘s local governance, providing specific services across city and county boundaries. These districts, such as the East Bay Municipal Utility District or the Orange County Fire Authority, ensure that essential services like water, sewage, and fire protection are managed across both urban and rural areas, regardless of municipal boundaries.
Additionally, California‘s unincorporated regions, particularly in the San Joaquin Valley and parts of Inyo County and Modoc County, are often agricultural lands that rely on county governance for law enforcement and infrastructure. For instance, Mono County manages roadways and emergency services in remote areas near the Eastern Sierra, where population density is too low to support formal municipalities.
